Note::defined¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

bool Note::defined() const noexcept

Ask Whether The Handle Contains A Note¶

defined() distinguishes an actual Note value from the sentinel returned by Note::undefined(). It tests the handle itself, not its text, shape, or element count. A scalar containing "" is defined. A matrix with a zero-sized axis is also defined. Only a handle with no backing Note storage reports false.

This distinction matters before calling operations that need geometry or cell storage. sizes(), size(), indexing, text transformations, and printing reject an undefined handle. The non-throwing metadata probes dim(), numel(), and empty() can inspect one, but their fallback values do not turn absence into a scalar or an empty array. Use defined() when that distinction controls program flow.

The query is constant-time, performs no allocation, never examines cell bytes, and is safe in validation and cleanup paths because it is noexcept.

Example 1: Undefined, Empty, And Empty Text Are Different¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined();
const auto empty_text = pluss::note::make("");
const auto empty_matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{}, std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 0});

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "absent=" << absent.defined() << '\n'
          << "empty text=" << empty_text.defined() << '\n'
          << "empty matrix=" << empty_matrix.defined() << '\n';

Output¶

absent=false
empty text=true
empty matrix=true

The latter two are usable Notes. One contains an empty string; the other has valid rank-2 geometry but no cells.

Example 2: Guard A Geometry-Dependent Operation¶

const auto value = pluss::Note::undefined();
if (!value.defined()) {
  std::cout << "no Note supplied\n";
} else {
  std::cout << value.sizes().size() << '\n';
}

Output¶

no Note supplied

Example 3: Absence Is Not Rank Zero¶

const auto value = pluss::Note::undefined();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "defined=" << value.defined()
          << " dim=" << value.dim()
          << " scalar=" << value.is_scalar() << '\n';

Output¶

defined=false dim=0 scalar=false

dim() uses zero as its non-throwing fallback, so is_scalar() additionally checks that the handle is defined.
